about: G5 end-to-end scenarios, hand-labelled 2026-09-18. Spray records are invented; every fact the truth relies on was read from the ONSSA cache (label crops, DAR) and the EU snapshot of 2026-09-13 (limit on the arrival date = harvest + 10 days), and is written in 'why'. 'verdict' is the answer a careful agronomist would give with full information; 'acceptable' lists other verdicts that are safe (never GREEN when the truth is not GREEN). eval/build_g5.py re-checks the cited label facts against the cache and fails if they changed.

scenarios.title: Clean citrus lot
scenarios.why: CORAGEN (chlorantraniliprole) registered on Agrumes, DAR 7: 20 Oct + 7 = 27 Oct < harvest 15 Dec. EU limit oranges 0.7 mg/kg (Reg. 2024/1355), approved. ADMIRAL 10 EC (pyriproxyfen) registered on Agrumes, DAR 30: 1 Oct + 30 = 31 Oct < 15 Dec. EU limit 0.7 mg/kg (Reg. 2023/1753), approved.

scenarios.title: Applied spray whose limit is at the detection level
scenarios.why: ACTARA 25 WG (thiamethoxam 25%) registered on Agrumes, DAR 28, interval respected. Thiamethoxam not approved in the EU; limit on oranges 0.01* mg/kg since 7 Mar 2026 (Reg. 2023/334): any detectable residue fails. Already sprayed, so options are for the next spray, not a replacement.

scenarios.title: Harvest planned before the waiting time ends
scenarios.why: ADMIRAL 10 EC DAR 30 on Agrumes: 1 Nov + 30 = 1 Dec, after the planned harvest of 20 Nov. The spray is done, so the fix is a later harvest (1 Dec), not another product. Pyriproxyfen limit itself is fine (0.7 mg/kg).

scenarios.title: Misspelled product name
scenarios.why: 'AKTARA 25 WG' is not in the ONSSA register; the grower most likely means ACTARA 25 WG. Until they confirm, the lot cannot be verified; it must not be GREEN and the name must not be silently corrected. RED is also acceptable (a system that confirms ACTARA from evidence would find the thiamethoxam problem).

scenarios.title: Product not registered for the crop
scenarios.why: ALAKAZAM 500 WG (flonicamid) is registered in Morocco for Agrumes only, not tomatoes: using it on tomatoes is off-label, whatever the EU limit (0.5 mg/kg). DECIS EXPERT (deltamethrin) registered on Tomate, DAR 3, limit 0.1 mg/kg: fine.

scenarios.title: Planned spray that would block the harvest
scenarios.why: Same thiamethoxam problem as g5-02, but the spray is planned for 1 Oct (after today, 17 Sep): the right answer is to replace it with a registered product against the same pest (leaf miner) that passes the EU rules.

scenarios.title: Import tolerance and a label name written differently
scenarios.why: MOVENTO 150 OD (spirotetramat) registered on Agrumes, DAR 21 respected; spirotetramat is not approved in the EU but has an import tolerance of 0.5 mg/kg on oranges: shippable with a warning (AMBER). KARATE 5 EC label says 'Lambda cyhalothrine' = EU 'Lambda-cyhalothrin', approved, 0.2 mg/kg on oranges, DAR 7 respected: fine. Ideal verdict AMBER; CANNOT_VERIFY is acceptable for a system that cannot map the label spelling.

scenarios.title: Spray log pasted from a spreadsheet, one bad line
scenarios.why: '31/11/2026' is not a date, so that line must be reported, not guessed. AGRIMEC GOLD (abamectin) on Tomate DAR 1: planned 25 Nov + 1 < 30 Nov; limit 0.015 mg/kg, approved. ACETA (acetamiprid) on Tomate DAR 3: 1 Nov + 3 < 30 Nov; limit 0.06 mg/kg, approved. The two readable lines are fine, but the unreadable line is a spray that happened (ALKADOR, imidacloprid) on an unknown date: the lot cannot be confirmed until the date is fixed. GREEN would hide a spray.
